functionalConvergenceAnalysis.centerpieceQuestion: Do two independent manufacturers require the same minimum functional abstractions for AIO laundry-combo diagnostics?
functionalConvergenceAnalysis.summary: Both manufacturers independently require integrated wash–dry orchestration on shared drum/controller and a non-vented sealed drying architecture distinct from vented_dryer. They diverge on dry heat/moisture-rejection implementation: Samsung uses heat-pump refrigerant cycle; Whirlpool uses resistive dry element + condenser duct + dual-fan ventless path. Functional convergence on integration; implementation divergence on dry thermal architecture.

samsungEvidence.provenance: §4-3 Smart Install steps 1–10; ULC cross-mode foam; shared motor 3C

whirlpoolEvidence.provenance: QSC steps 1–14 with step 10 dry blower after spin; F5E4 between cycles; Component Activation Dry Heater & Combo Fan; single ACU

integrated_laundry_orchestration.convergenceRationale: Both manufacturers independently document unified controller, shared drum/motor, sequential wash→dry service verification without load transfer, and cross-mode door/cycle dependencies. This is functional convergence — not component similarity.

samsungEvidence.dryArchitecture: BLDC compressor 3CA, EVA thermistors, dehumidifying kit NC, supplemental dry heater

whirlpoolEvidence.dryArchitecture: Resistive dry heater TEST #15, dry blower #17, vent fan #13, vent baffle #14, condenser duct — no compressor/refrigerant

sharedFunctionalLayer.description: Both require sealed/ventless moisture rejection without vented_dryer exhaust_path terminal; both use condensation pathway; both have sealed airflow through drum with dry thermal control and dry NTC

implementationDivergence.description: Samsung primary heat transfer via refrigerant loop; Whirlpool primary heat via resistive element on air stream through condenser duct
